1.

The petitioner is seeking compensation in the wake of Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed by police corresponding to the investigation carried out in case FIR No. 353/18 U/s 279/337 IPC registered at Police Station: Mahendra Park with regard to Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 21.08.2018 at about 11:05 pm at GTK Depot Red Light, Opposite Sanjay Enclave,
Jahangir Puri, Delhi, involving Tata ACE bearing registration no. DL1LT0975 (offending vehicle)
being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner.

DAR filed by police, was treated as claim petition under Section 166(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act').
2.
According to DAR, on 21.08.2018, the petitioner/injured and his friend namely Sh. Deepak were returning to their respective houses after finishing their duties.

At about 11:15 pm, when the petitioner was crossing the GTK Depot Red Light, Opposite Sanjay Enclave, Jahangir Puri, Delhi,
MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 he saw a man getting slipped from his motorcycle and he rushed towards him for his help and

at that time, offending vehicle which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
came from behind and hit him with a great force, as a result of which, he fell down on the road and received grievous injuries.
He was taken to BJRM Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi where he was medically examined.
FIR No. 353/18 was registered at PS. Mahendra Park with regard to the accident.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited/respondent no. 3 during the period in question.

sentences.text: 3. In their joint written statements, the respondent no. 1 & 2 i.e. driver and registered owner raised preliminary objection that the accident in question was not caused by the offending vehicle.

It has been claimed that respondent no. 1 had purchased the second hand offending vehicle through M/s.
Manish Auto Deals and paid a sum of Rs. 2,60,000/ in cash for insurance, Permit, Tax and RC transfer and other expenses.
It has been further claimed that they had never issued cheque to respondent no. 3.
It was further claimed that respondent no. 1 was having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and thus, they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
On merits, they denied the averments made in the DAR and prayed for its dismissal.
MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 4.

In its written statement, the respondent no. 3/insurance company claimed that policy bearing no.
3003/142542959/00/B00 having validity from 12.01.2018 to 11.01.2019 in the name of Sh. Sanjeev was issued by it for offending vehicle against cheque no. 06712 dated 10.01.2018 and validity of the policy was subject to realization of aforesaid cheque.
It has been further claimed that the said cheque was dishonoured upon its presentation and thus, no premium was received against the said policy.
On the bases of these averments, it has been claimed that it has no liability to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It has denied the averments made in the DAR and prayed for its dismissal.
5. From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 28.05.2019 passed by my Ld.

DL1LT0975, owned by Neo Hospitality and insured with ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co Ltd?

3. Relief.
MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 6.
In support of his claim, the petitioner has examined two witnesses i.e. himself as PW1 and PW2 Sh. Deepak Sharma(eyewitness) and his evidence was closed vide order dated 03.02.2020.

On the other hand, the respondents no. 1 & 2 have examined one witness i.e. respondent no. 1 as R1W1 and respondent no. 3/insurance company has examined one witness i.e. R2W1(sicR3W1) Sh. Gautam Bhatnagar and closed their respective evidence on 22.08.2022.
7. I have heard the arguments addressed by ld counsels for the parties.

My findings on the issues are as under:
8.

For the purpose of this issue, the testimonies of PW1 Sh. Nafees(injured himself) and PW2 Sh.
Deepak Sharma (eyewitness) are relevant.

In their respective evidence by way of affidavits (Ex.
PW1/A & Ex. PW2/1), they have deposed on the similar lines of averments made in the DAR.

PW1 has relied upon the following documents: S.No. Description of documents Remarks 1. Copy of his 10th class Certificate Ex. PW1/1 3. His original treatment record Ex. PW1/3(colly)
4. Copy of FIR Ex. PW1/4(colly)
5. Copy of his bank passbook Ex. PW1/5(colly) MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS.
Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 9.
During cross examination on behalf of respondent no. 1, petitioner admitted that after the accident, he had become unconscious.
He deposed that he had not seen the registration number of the offending vehicle.
He further deposed that he had seen the offending vehicle first time in police station after two month of the accident.
He further deposed that he had seen the driver/respondent no. 1 first time in the court at the time of filing of DAR.
He deposed that his friend Deepak who was accompanying him at the time of accident had pointed out towards the driver Sh. Sanjeev.

He Mohd. Nafees vs Sh. Sanjeev on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86918958/

sentences.text: He deposed that one Sachin had called the police on telephone and Sachin had reached at the spot of accident after the accident.
He further deposed that his friend Deepak had taken him to the hospital.
He denied the suggestion that no accident had taken place with offending vehicle.
He further denied the suggestion that Deepak had reached at the hospital later on.
He denied the suggestion that some other vehicle came had hit him.

He further denied the suggestion that accident had taken place due to his negligence as he had not bothered for the traffic moving on the road while rushing towards the man who had slipped on the road for helping him.

10. During crossexamination on behalf of respondent no. 1 & 3, PW2 Deepak deposed that he did not remember the exact date of accident but it was the month of August 2018 at 11:00 to 11:30 PM.
He deposed that he did not make a call to the police and somebody from the hospital made a MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 call to the police.
He denied the suggestion that he was not present at the spot.
He further denied the suggestion that he had reached at the hospital only after the accident.
He denied the suggestion that he did not know which vehicle had caused the accident.
He further denied the suggestion that offending vehicle has not caused the accident.
11. It is evident from the testimonies of PW1 & PW2 that respondents could not impeach their testimony through litmus test of cross examination.
Said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of crossexamination.
Even otherwise, PW1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely against respondent no.1.
Furthermore, it is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 353/18 u/s 279/337 IPC was registered at PS. Mahendra Park with regard to accident in question.

Copy of said FIR (Ex. PW1/4), would show that same was registered on 22.08.2018(accident being caused on 21.08.2018 at about 11:05 PM) on the basis of DD Entry No. 57B with regard to accident call received in PS. Mahendra Park on 21.08.2018.

The respondents no. 1 & 2 have failed to substantiate the plea that petitioner had any kind of ill will or enmity against them so as to falsely implicate respondent no. 1 in criminal case or to depose falsely against them during the course of inquiry.
12.

As already noted above, the respondent no. 1 & 2 have examined one witness i.e. respondent no.
1 himself as R1W1 in order to rebut the case of petitioner.

He has deposed in his evidence by way of MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 affidavit Ex. R1W1/A that accident had taken place due to the negligence of petitioner himself as he was crossing the road without caring for traffic moving on the road at the time of accident.
However, the respondent no. 1 has claimed that the offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident.
Respondent no.1 further deposed that he was having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Respondent no. 1 has relied upon the copy of RC of offending vehicle as Ex. R1W1/1; Copy of fitness certificate of offending vehicle as Ex. R1W1/2 and copy of his driving licence Ex. R1W1/3.
During his crossexamination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he did not have any receipt showing premium paid for insurance policy qua the offending vehicle.
He further deposed that he had not issued any letter to the person to whom he had paid the amount of premium for issuing the receipt of premium of insurance policy.
He deposed that he had received the insurance policy Ex. R2W1/1.
He denied the suggestion that cheque of premium was issued by him.

He denied Mohd. Nafees vs Sh. Sanjeev on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86918958/
4 the suggestion that he was aware about the dishonour of cheque issued against premium of policy of offending vehicle.

During his crossexamination on behalf of petitioner, he deposed that he had purchased the offending vehicle from Manish Auto Dealer at Moti Nagar, Delhi for a sum of Rs.
2,60,000/.
He denied the suggestion that the accident had taken place due to his fault and negligence.
MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 13.
Ld. Counsel for the respondents no. 1 & 2 vehemently argued that the petitioner has failed to prove negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 in causing the accident.
For this purpose, he has heavily relied upon the testimony of R1W1 as discussed above.

On the other hand, Ld. counsel for petitioner argued that the testimony of respondent no. 1 recorded as R1W1 should not be believed as FIR was registered against him and he is facing trial in the criminal case.
14. As regards the testimony of the witness examined as R1W1, it may be noted that he had simply deposed that petitioner himself was solely negligent and responsible for the accident.

It may be noted here that during crossexamination of PW1, the Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 1 gave suggestion that some other vehicle had hit the petitioner on the date of accident which was ofcourse denied by the said witness.

It clearly shows that the respondent no.1 has raised two inconsistent pleas in his WS, he claimed that accident had taken place due to sole negligence of petitioner because he was crossing the road without taking care of traffic moving on the road.
On the other side, he gave suggestion to PW1 that some other vehicle had hit him on the date of accident.

Thus,
there is no reason to discard the testimony of PW1 and PW2 made on oath.

15. The very fact that respondent no. 1 was chargesheeted(which is part of DAR) by the police for offences punishable u/s. 279/338 IPC & MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 146/196 M.V. Act would further show that Investigating Agency also concluded after completion of the investigation that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver(respondent no.1 herein) and same also points out towards the fact that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner herein.

16. Apart from above, copy of MLC (which is part of DAR) of injured prepared at BJRM Hospital,
Jahangir Puri, Delhi shows that he had been removed to said hospital on 21.08.2018 at about 11:30 pm with alleged history of RTA.
On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned therein.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in a motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no challenge to the said document from the side of respondents including insurance company.

17. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of pre ponderence of probabilities that he had sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 21.08.2018 at about 11:05 pm at Mohd. GTK Depot Red Light, Opposite Sanjay Enclave, Jahangir Puri, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
18. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
MEDICAL EXPENSES 19.

The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex. PW1/A) that after the accident,
he had been taken to BJRM Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi and thereafter, he was shifted to JPN Hospital, Max Hospital and then, finally he was shifted to Sir Ganga Ram Hospital on 23.08.2018 and from where he was discharged on 13.09.2018.
He deposed that he had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

He has relied upon his medical treatment record Ex. PW1/3(colly).
20.
It is relevant to note that the injured is found to have received treatment from Sir Ganga Ram Hospital under EWS category and no amount was paid by him in the said hospital during his treatment.
The said MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 fact is duly corroborated by the bills filed by him on record.
In view of the above, no amount can be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
LOSS OF INCOME 21.

The petitioner has categorically deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/A) that at the time of accident, he was working n Delhi Home Guard as Constable and deployed as Marshal in DTC Bus and was drawing monthly salary of Rs. 20,000/.
For this, he has relied upon copy of his bank passbook Ex. PW1/5.
He deposed that he could not attend his duty for about three months due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

22. Apart from the treatment record Ex. PW1/3(colly), the petitioner has failed to file any other medical treatment record in order to show the exact period upto which he had received the medical treatment.
Nevertheless, it can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
As per discharge summary of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital(which is part of Ex. PW1/3 colly), the petitioner is found to have sustained head injury with bifrontal contusions.

Thus,
appropriate amount should be awarded to him under the head of loss of income.

It is relevant to note here that although, the petitioner has failed to file any document showing the exact period upto which he had received the treatment, however, after considering the nature of injuries sustained by MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 him, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work for a period of 3 months or so.

sentences.text: Apart from the bald statement made by the petitioner that he was earning Rs. 20,000/ per month, no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove his monthly income at the time of accident in question.
However, Ld. Counsel for petitioner has relied upon copy of bank passbook Ex. PW1/5 of petitioner wherein an entry of Rs. 20,325/ was being reflected.
He argued that said amount was being received by the petitioner as his salary of the relevant month.

It is relevant to note here that it is not anywhere mentioned on the Ex. PW1/5 that from which source, it has been received by the petitioner in his account which creates doubt about the authenticity of said entry.
Thus, I am not inclined to accept the monthly income of petitioner as mentioned in the said document Ex. PW1/5 or Rs. 20,000/ per month.
However, the petitioner has filed copy of his 10 th class certificate.
Thus, his loss of income has to be assessed while taking the income of a Matriculate person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question.
The minimum wages of a matriculate person were Rs. 16,858/ per month as on the date of accident which is 21.08.2018.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 50,574/ (Rs. 16,858/ x 3) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.
MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 PAIN AND SUFFERING 24.

Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the matter titled as " Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors."
passed in appeal bearing no. MAC.APP 518/2010 decided on 05.07.12, has held as under: " It is difficult to measure the pain and suffering in terms of money which is suffered by a victim on account of serious injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident.

entities.text: Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the compensation is required to be paid for pain and suffering an attempt must be made to award compensation which may have some objective relation with the pain and suffering underwent by the victim.

For this purpose, the Claims Tribunal and the Courts normally consider the nature of injury; the part of the body where the injuries were sustained, surgeries, if any, underwent by the victim, confinement in the hospital and the duration of treatment".
25.
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/A) that he had sustained grievous injuries in the accident in question.
Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings and mental shock on account of the accident in question.

Keeping in view the medical treatment record of petitioner available on record and the nature of injuries suffered by him, I hereby award a sum of Rs. 50,000/ towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.
MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 LOSS OF GENERAL AMENITIES & ENJOYMENT OF LIFE 26.
As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries due to the accident.
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.

In view of the nature of injuries suffered by him, I award a notional sum of Rs. 50,000/
towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner.

CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES Mohd. Nafees vs Sh. Sanjeev on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86918958/
7 27.
During the course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioners argued that petitioner had spent considerable amount on his special diet, conveyance and attendant.
It is relevant to note here that the petitioner has failed to lead any cogent evidence to prove the amount, if any spent on special diet, conveyance and attendant as aforesaid by him.
At the same time, it cannot be overlooked that petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

Thus, he would have taken special rich protein diet for his speedy recovery and would have also incurred considerable amount towards conveyance charges while commuting to the concerned hospital as OPD patient for his regular check up & follow up during the period of his medical treatment.

He would have been definitely helped by some person either outsider or from his family, to perform his daily activities as also while MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 visiting the hospital during the course of his medical treatment.
In these facts and circumstances, I hereby award a notional sum of Rs. 10,000/ each for special diet, conveyance charges and attendant charges to the petitioner.

Thus, the total compensation is assessed as under:
1. Loss of income Rs. 50,574/
2. Pain and suffering Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of general amenities and Rs. 50,000/ enjoyment of life 4. Conveyance, special diet & Rs. 30,000/ attendant charges Total Rs. 1,80,574/ Rounded off to Rs. 1,81,000/
28.
Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

Ld. Counsel for insurance company sought to avoid the liability of insurance company to pay the compensation amount on the ground that the cheque given by the insured towards premium payment was dishonoured and subsequently the insurance policy was cancelled.

29. In order to prove its defence respondent no. 3 has examined R2W1(sicR3W1) Sh. Gautam Bhatnagar, Manager(Legal), ICICI Lombard MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 17.02.2023 General Insurance Co. Ltd who deposed that policy bearing no.
3003/142542959/00/B00 having validity from 12.01.2018 to 11.01.2019 was issued in the name of Sh. Sanjeev for offending vehicle against a cheque bearing no. 067121 dated 10.01.2018 for a sum of Rs. 11,133/ and the validity of the policy was subject to realization of said cheque.

He further deposed that the said cheque was presented with the bank of insurance company and the same was received unpaid from the bank and thus, no premium was received against the said policy and consequently, the said policy was cancelled immediately.
He further deposed that a notice dated 27.01.2018 was issued to the insured as well as to the Transport Authority on 31.01.2018 that the policy was cancelled due to dishnour of cheque.
He further deposed that due to this reason only, the police has filed the chargesheet u/s. 279/338 IPC & 146/196 M.V. Act against the respondent no. 1.

He has relied upon the copy of policy Ex. R2W1/1, original cheque and its return memo Ex. R2W1/2 & Ex. R2W1/3 respectively, copy of notice dated 27.01.2018 to the insured and its delivery proof Ex.

sentences.text: Now, it is the submission of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurance Company that the owner of the lorry had issued a cheque dated 25.10.2013 for the policy covering the period 26.10.2013 to 25.10.2014, and the said cheque was returned by the banker on 30.10.2013 and immediately, the policy was cancelled from the inception on 07.11.2013 and that the intimation was sent on 11.11.2013 to the insured and the Regional Transport Officer, but the accident had occurred on 13.12.2013 and the insured had sufficient time and opportunity as to whether the vehicle was permitted to drive with valid insurance or not, whereas he failed to do so.

Therefore, on the date of accident, according to the learned counsel appearing for the MACP No. 105/19; FIR No. 353/18; PS. Mahendra Park DOD:
17.02.2023 appellant/Insurance Company, there was no insurer insured relationship between the appellant/Insurance Company and the owner of the lorry, and therefore, the question of paying the compensation does not arise.

Though the Tribunal had accepted that, on the date of accident, there was no contract of insurance between the insurer and the owner, yet, the Tribunal had directed the appellant/Insurance Company to pay the compensation amounts and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

Hence, the said direction of the Tribunal is liable to be set aside and consequently, the Insurance Company may be exonerated from paying the compensation amounts"
